core_obligations: Reduce to a scheme (proof lines 886-890): after shrinking the space one may assume it is an integral Noetherian scheme, since the prime divisor meets the schematic locus.

Compare the local rings (proof lines 890-894): for the generic point of the divisor the henselian local ring is the henselization of the local ring of the scheme at that point, so it suffices and is necessary to prove the equality of the lengths of the quotients by the principal ideal over the two local rings.

Conclude by flatness (proof lines 894-900): the length of the quotient is unchanged under the flat local ring homomorphism from the local ring to its henselization, by the algebra lemma on lengths after flat base change, which gives the desired equality.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the schematic locus, where the space is an integral Noetherian scheme.
Identify the henselian local ring as a henselization and restate the problem as an equality of lengths.
Use the change-of-length formula for a flat local extension.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a rational function on a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space and a prime divisor meeting the schematic locus, the order of vanishing defined in the chapter agrees with the classical order of vanishing for schemes (statement lines 876-884). The proof (proof lines 886-902) reduces to an integral Noetherian scheme, identifies the henselian local ring as a henselization, restates the assertion as an equality of lengths of quotients, and concludes by the invariance of length under a flat local extension. H2: a three-step reduction with three inputs, written out in full.
